Besides (i) adding a validated external dependency and (ii) weakening the root contract, a prover may keep the root contract unchanged and add internal AF proof children deriving the missing assertion R (bijectivity of the explicit Pi_delta, existence/uniqueness of (u_delta,h_delta), and identification of its first component with the upstream u_delta) directly from the already allowed epsilon-C*-algebra axioms. Whether that derivation is difficult or currently absent does not make it logically impossible, and node 1.7 supplies no impossibility or independence argument excluding it. Thus the conclusions 'requires exactly one' and 'without (i) or (ii), node 1 must remain unproved' overclaim what the dependency audit establishes; the audit establishes only that the current children do not prove R.
